key_insight: The paper shows that noisy agent execution traces can be turned into useful optimization signals by extracting the structural path to failure and isolating the true causal factors. In simple terms: instead of learning from all logs, the optimizer learns from the important parts that actually explain what went wrong.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of using long-horizon agent traces for reflection-based optimization, where trace datasets are often redundant, heterogeneous, and full of irrelevant steps. These properties make optimization inefficient and can cause overfitting to low-value failures rather than real root causes.
method: Analyzes agent trajectories structurally to separate meaningful failure patterns from noisy, repetitive, or irrelevant trace content.
Performs causal extraction to identify the steps or decisions most responsible for a failure, rather than treating the whole trajectory as equally informative.
Uses the extracted root-cause signals to support more efficient reflection-based agent optimization.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means agent debugging and policy improvement can become more targeted, data-efficient, and robust. It can reduce wasted optimization effort on noisy traces and improve the quality of reflection-based learning for long-horizon agents.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline showing raw noisy traces transforming into structured causal summaries
Highlighted trajectory diagram with irrelevant steps faded out and root-cause steps emphasized
Flowchart of the optimization loop: trace collection -> structural analysis -> causal extraction -> agent improvement

paper_title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
paper_authors: Ying Chang, Jiahang Xu, Xuan Feng, Chenyuan Yang, Peng Cheng
